title: The rope and the snake
english: As a rope not clearly seen in the dark is imagined to be a snake, a trickle of water and other things, so the Self is imagined to be many things.
When the rope is seen clearly, the imagining stops, and there is only the rope, with nothing second to it. So it is when the Self is known for certain.
translator: Working translation for Atman from the Sanskrit, awaiting review
edition: Sanskrit: Āgamaśāstra, ed. V. G. Āpaṭe, Ānandāśrama Sanskrit Series 10 (Pune, 1921), as input on GRETIL
notes: The snake was never there, and the rope never changed. Advaita calls an error like this prātibhāsika: an appearance that lasts only until it is seen through. The village, its chores and its people are not that kind of error; they are real for living in. [C1] [S1]
